scope: Static review only; no harness, scanner, fixture, command, or subprocess was invoked.
axes: host probes and descendants cannot escape the measurement boundary
receipts bind the executed tool and runner
assessment: The transcript parser is AST-only, but the planned measurement path executes the selected scanner module. Safe entry is currently source/artifact reads only. Later measurement requires a sealed, explicitly trusted tool path and input-root confinement; the resource/time limits alone are not a sandbox.

findings.title: The selected scanner is executable Python, not inert input
findings.exploit_path: replay.py accepts any regular file resolving inside the repository as --tool. Oracle mode invokes the round-21 measurement runner, whose wrapper imports the selected path with importlib and calls exec_module. A malicious or unintended in-repository .py therefore executes at import with the invoking user's environment and filesystem permissions; -I does not prevent that.
evidence: tools/mado-tripwire.py:2101-2114 compiles transcript source with PyCF_ONLY_AST; this establishes input parsing behavior, not safety of arbitrary --tool code
findings.impact: If an unreviewed tool path is accepted, its top-level code can access private files, environment secrets, or initiate host/network actions even though JSONL payload code is not evaluated.
findings.smallest_remediation: Before any run, allow only the explicitly selected scanner path(s) and require their independently sealed SHA-256. If candidate code is not trusted, run it in a separately authorized unprivileged, no-network, read-only fixture sandbox; do not treat -I, timeout, or RLIMIT_AS as isolation.

findings.title: Round-21 fixture path resolution can reach private sessions
findings.exploit_path: The reference oracle runner joins unvalidated expected.json case.fixture values to ROOT and reads/scans the resulting path. A traversal value can point to ~/.omp/agent/sessions; tools/mado-tripwire.py explicitly permits that subtree in refuse_path. If a writable local expected.json and its adjacent expected.sha256 are both replaced, the scanner can read private JSONL despite this wave's no-session rule.
evidence: .ufo/waves/round-21/oracle/measure.py:49-60 reads the adjacent digest and uses ROOT / case['fixture'] without containment validation
tools/mado-tripwire.py:2575-2589 permits paths within ~/.omp/agent/sessions; 2593-2619 discovers JSONL beneath the supplied path
.ufo/waves/round-22/audit-contract.json:7 and audit-clarifications.md:5-8 explicitly require path/symlink rejection for C2, but no new C1 harness implementation was present at inspection
findings.impact: A later harness run could read and classify private session material and include sensitive command/path fragments in its receipt. A colocated digest sidecar is not an independent authenticity anchor if both files are writable.
findings.smallest_remediation: Derive fixture paths only from validated case IDs under the sealed inputs directory; reject absolute, dot/dotdot, symlink components, and any resolved path outside that directory. Pin the manifest digest outside the mutable harness tree before running.

findings.title: Replay records tool drift but does not fail on it
findings.exploit_path: replay.py hashes --tool before launch and after completion, but returns the runner's exit code without comparing those hashes. It records the runner hash only before execution and does not check it against an independently sealed digest. A file swap during a later run can therefore accompany an exit 0/1 receipt unless a downstream consumer independently rejects the mismatch.
evidence: .ufo/waves/round-22/replay.py:145-160 records hashes; 161-169 returns exit_code without enforcing equality or a pinned runner digest
findings.impact: The returned process status can be mistaken for a result tied to stable, approved bytes; the receipt exposes the mismatch but does not itself fail closed.
findings.smallest_remediation: Require exact sealed tool and runner digests before launch, recheck after, and force exit 2 on any mismatch.

findings.title: Per-case timeout does not guarantee descendant cleanup
findings.exploit_path: The new replay driver starts a process group and kills it on its own aggregate timeout, but on normal completion it does not terminate remaining group members. The nested round-21 oracle runner uses subprocess.run(timeout=15) for the scanner, which only kills/waits for that direct child. An imported tool that starts a detached/stdio-closed descendant can outlive a successful per-case run.
evidence: .ufo/waves/round-22/replay.py:75-97 kills the process group only in the outer TimeoutExpired branch
.ufo/waves/round-21/oracle/measure.py:28-38 invokes subprocess.run with timeout but no new session or group cleanup
findings.impact: A descendant may continue with the user's privileges after the receipt is emitted, including filesystem or host-probe actions.
findings.smallest_remediation: Run each measurement child in its own session and reap/terminate its process group on every exit path, or constrain execution to a sandbox that denies process creation.
